# Orca static-fee mathematical reference

This project pins `orca_whirlpools_core = 1.0.4` and `orca_whirlpools_macros = 1.0.4`. Both exact published package manifests declare **Apache-2.0**, and both were published on 2025-02-21. Copyright 2022 Orca Foundation. The [Apache 2.0 license text](LICENSE-APACHE-2.0.txt) is included here; upstream attribution and notices must accompany redistributed material as applicable.

The package archives were obtained from the official crates.io distribution and their SHA-256 checksums matched the crates.io version API. The core quote and pool facade source blobs were independently compared with official source at [commit 1ef659d8107f9c81081752ffb5fdde157eeddbe2](https://github.com/orca-so/whirlpools/tree/1ef659d8107f9c81081752ffb5fdde157eeddbe2), whose [LICENSE](https://github.com/orca-so/whirlpools/blob/1ef659d8107f9c81081752ffb5fdde157eeddbe2/LICENSE) and package metadata identify Apache 2.0. The immutable checksums and verified blob hashes are in [orca-1.0.4-provenance.json](orca-1.0.4-provenance.json).

The published crate VCS metadata refers to commit `6e147b29cdacbaf261447d96531071fd99435a63`, which GitHub returned as unavailable, and the core metadata marks the publishing tree dirty. We therefore identify the dependency by its exact release archive checksum, not by claiming it is a clean build from that unavailable commit. The checked quote/pool source blobs match the accessible Apache reference commit. This is a dependency provenance record, not a legal opinion or an audit of every transitive dependency.

Current Orca releases have different license terms. An automatic version upgrade is inappropriate: both direct and macro versions are pinned exactly. The reference disables the default `floats` feature and does not enable WebAssembly bindings. Upstream declares Rust edition 2021 and does not specify an MSRV; this repository's CI determines compatibility with its pinned Rust toolchain.

The wrapper accepts only fixed tick arrays, static fee tiers and legacy SPL Token math. It rejects adaptive fee seeds, missing or discontinuous arrays, invalid exact-in amounts, inconsistent tick/price inputs and partial input consumption. The result is **CANDIDATE** integer mathematics. It does not establish that the historical core exactly matches an upgraded current program, that RPC account contexts are coherent, that a transaction will execute, or that a trade is profitable. Those require current-deployment comparisons and the existing simulation/qualification gates.

## Bounded tick-window integration requirement

The 1.0.4 high-level `swap_quote_by_input_token` helper uses global price limits. With a finite supplied tick window, its swap loop can repeatedly revisit the same boundary without consuming input. A regression test exposed this behavior with an exhausted window. This project therefore **does not call that helper**: its adapter supplies an explicit window-derived price limit to `compute_swap`, rejects an empty directional interval and requires complete requested-input consumption. Every directionally reachable initialized-tick liquidity transition is checked for underflow/overflow before entering the historical core, whose transition arithmetic is otherwise unchecked. Regression cases retain large-input exhaustion in both directions, exact boundaries and malformed liquidity changes. This mitigation does not replace current-deployment qualification.

## Macro update reviewed on 2026-09-13

The proposed `orca_whirlpools_macros` 1.0.5 update is excluded from automatic dependency updates. At upstream publishing commit `7361eac19e3220d2dcade932ea0c4ce97bf6e44b`, the [exact 1.0.5 package manifest](https://github.com/orca-so/whirlpools/blob/7361eac19e3220d2dcade932ea0c4ce97bf6e44b/rust-sdk/macros/Cargo.toml) specifies `license-file = "../../LICENSE"`. The [license at that same commit](https://github.com/orca-so/whirlpools/blob/7361eac19e3220d2dcade932ea0c4ce97bf6e44b/LICENSE) identifies the Orca License effective February 27, 2025, with terms distinct from the Apache-2.0 release pinned here. Successful compilation does not resolve that change.

Both exact 1.0.4 pins and their verified archive identities remain unchanged. Dependabot ignores macro versions `>=1.0.5`; adopting a later release requires an explicit dependency and license review with a fresh archive provenance record. This review checked the cited upstream source and license, not the 1.0.5 release archive.
